# Sirach Chapter 1 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Sirach 1 (30 verses)
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 18

---

## Disagreement 001 — v.1: "remains forever" vs. "endures forever"

**EMET:** "with him it remains forever"
**LOGOS:** "with him it endures forever"
**PNEUMA:** "it belongs to him forever"
**Issue:** Greek menei eis ton aiona. EMET and LOGOS both capture "abiding/remaining." PNEUMA shifts to ownership framing. Consensus: "endures forever."

---

## Disagreement 002 — v.4: "understanding prudence" vs. "prudent understanding"

**EMET:** "understanding prudence from eternity"
**LOGOS:** "prudent understanding from the beginning"
**PNEUMA:** "understanding present from the very beginning"
**Issue:** Greek synesis phronimou. EMET renders as two nouns; LOGOS uses adjective-noun; PNEUMA paraphrases. "Eternity" vs. "the beginning" for ap' archēs. Consensus: "prudent understanding from the very beginning."

---

## Disagreement 003 — v.5: Inclusion/exclusion decision

**EMET:** Includes v.5 with translator's note flagging textual uncertainty
**LOGOS:** Includes v.5 without flag
**PNEUMA:** Includes v.5 without flag
**Issue:** This verse is absent from key manuscript witnesses. EMET's note is correct procedure. Consensus: include with notation.

---

## Disagreement 004 — v.8: Description of God

**EMET:** "greatly to be feared, sitting upon his throne"
**LOGOS:** "the awe-inspiring one seated on his throne"
**PNEUMA:** "the awesome Lord, enthroned above all"
**Issue:** Greek phoberōs sphodra. EMET is most literal. LOGOS is elegant. PNEUMA adds "above all" without Greek support. Consensus: "greatly to be feared, seated on his throne."

---

## Disagreement 005 — v.10: "with all flesh" vs. "among all people"

**EMET:** "she is with all flesh according to his gift"
**LOGOS:** "she dwells with all flesh according to his bounty"
**PNEUMA:** "she lives among all people by his gift"
**Issue:** Greek meta pasēs sarkos. "Flesh" is literal; LOGOS adds "dwells." PNEUMA softens "flesh" to "people." Consensus: "she is present among all people according to his bounty" — splitting.

---

## Disagreement 006 — v.11: "crown of rejoicing" vs. "festive crown"

**EMET:** "a crown of rejoicing"
**LOGOS:** "a festive crown"
**PNEUMA:** "a crown of joy"
**Issue:** Greek stephanos agalliamatos. EMET is most literal (agalliamat- = exultation/rejoicing). LOGOS interprets. Consensus: "a festive crown of joy."

---

## Disagreement 007 — v.14: "beginning of wisdom" vs. "root of wisdom"

**EMET:** "The beginning of wisdom is to fear the Lord"
**LOGOS:** "The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord"
**PNEUMA:** "To revere the Lord — that is where wisdom begins"
**Issue:** Vaticanus reads archē sophias ("beginning"). Some manuscripts have rhiza ("root"). v.20 also has "root." EMET follows Vaticanus strictly. LOGOS conflates with v.20. Consensus: follow Vaticanus — "The beginning of wisdom is to fear the Lord" at v.14; "root" at v.20.

---

## Disagreement 008 — v.14: "created in the womb" vs. "woven into those who are faithful from their birth"

**EMET:** "with the faithful she was created in the womb"
**LOGOS:** "her branches are long life" (conflated v.14 with v.20)
**PNEUMA:** "woven into those who are faithful from their very birth"
**Issue:** EMET preserves the image of wisdom being co-created with the faithful. LOGOS dropped this phrase by confusion with v.20. Consensus: EMET reading preserved.

---

## Disagreement 009 — v.16: "fullness of wisdom" vs. "to be filled with wisdom"

**EMET:** "Fullness of wisdom is to fear the Lord"
**LOGOS:** "To be filled with wisdom is to fear the Lord"
**PNEUMA:** "To be saturated with the fear of the Lord — that is true wisdom"
**Issue:** Greek plēsmonē sophias. EMET treats as noun; LOGOS/PNEUMA as verbal idea. Consensus: "To be filled with wisdom is to fear the Lord."

---

## Disagreement 010 — v.16: "makes them drink" vs. "inebriates them"

**EMET:** "she makes them drink from the fruit of her deeds"
**LOGOS:** "she inebriates them with her fruits"
**PNEUMA:** "she fills those who hold her with the fruit of all she has to give"
**Issue:** Greek methyskei = "makes drunk/inebriates." EMET avoids drunkenness metaphor; LOGOS embraces it. Consensus: "she inebriates them with her fruits" — the intoxication image is intentional in Ben Sira.

---

## Disagreement 011 — v.18: "causing peace and full health to flourish" vs. "from it bloom peace"

**EMET:** "causing peace and full health to flourish"
**LOGOS:** "making peace and wholesome health to flourish"
**PNEUMA:** "from it bloom peace and the fullness of health"
**Issue:** Minor word choice. All capture the meaning. Consensus: "causing peace and wholesome health to flourish."

---

## Disagreement 012 — v.21: Textual status

**EMET:** Includes with translator's note
**LOGOS:** Includes without flag
**PNEUMA:** Includes without flag
**Issue:** v.21 ("the fear of the Lord drives away sins") is absent from Sinaiticus. EMET's caution is noted. Consensus: include.

---

## Disagreement 013 — v.22: "unjust man" vs. "hot-tempered person"

**EMET:** "An unjust man will not be able to justify himself"
**LOGOS:** "A wrathful person cannot be justified"
**PNEUMA:** "A hotheaded person has no case to make"
**Issue:** Greek adikos = "unjust" vs. context suggesting the one with unrighteous anger. LOGOS and PNEUMA read contextually. Consensus: "A hot-tempered person" following the thematic context of anger management.

---

## Disagreement 014 — v.23: "gladness will burst forth" vs. "joy will break out"

**EMET:** "gladness will burst forth for him"
**LOGOS:** "joy will break out for him"
**PNEUMA:** "joy will burst out like dawn"
**Issue:** PNEUMA adds "like dawn" — not in Greek. EMET and LOGOS are both accurate. Consensus: "joy will burst forth for him."

---

## Disagreement 015 — v.25: "sayings of instruction" vs. "wise sayings"

**EMET:** "sayings of instruction" (logoi paideias)
**LOGOS:** "wise sayings"
**PNEUMA:** "instructive sayings"
**Issue:** Greek logoi paideias = "words of education/instruction." EMET most literal. Consensus: "proverbs of instruction."

---

## Disagreement 016 — v.27: "faithfulness and meekness" vs. "loyalty and humility"

**EMET:** "he delights in faithfulness and meekness"
**LOGOS:** "faithfulness and humility are his delight"
**PNEUMA:** "what pleases him is loyalty and a humble heart"
**Issue:** Greek pistis kai prautēs. Pistis = faithfulness/loyalty; prautēs = meekness/gentleness/humility. Consensus: "faithfulness and humility."

---

## Disagreement 017 — v.29: "play the hypocrite" vs. "don't play a role"

**EMET:** "Do not play the hypocrite before the eyes of men"
**LOGOS:** "Do not be a hypocrite before others"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't play a role for others to see"
**Issue:** Greek hypokrinesthai = to play a role (theatrical term). EMET adds "before the eyes of men" (present in some manuscripts). Consensus: "Do not play the hypocrite before others."

---

## Disagreement 018 — v.30: "in the midst of the congregation" vs. "before the assembly"

**EMET:** "cast you down in the midst of the congregation"
**LOGOS:** "bring you low in the assembly"
**PNEUMA:** "bring you down before the whole community"
**Issue:** Greek en mesō ekklēsias. Consensus: "cast you down in the midst of the assembly."

---
